reasons.message: Correctness and ownership: the quote route uses the existing BasketInput, authenticated actor, and price_basket and only serializes its result. B/store/api.py:28-30 has the same request flow and calculation; neither duplicates pricing or writes database state.

Verification: A checks exact quote/order error parity and database snapshots, alongside independent expected totals and forged price/tier checks. B/tests/test_quotes.py:90 supplies comparable checks; B additionally changes stored prices/tier while A separately checks the exact shipping boundary. These are useful complementary cases without a material overall quality difference.

uncertainties: Correctness review was static; no candidate tests were executed and report claims of passing runs were not independently confirmed.

reasons.message: Correctness and maintainability: the added endpoint is identical to B/store/api.py:28-30. Both use the same schema, authentication and shared read-only settlement function and preserve the original order routes.

Verification: A's shared assertion checks independent amounts, repeated quote snapshots, and subsequent order parity. B/tests/test_quotes.py:27-53 performs equivalent checks in a scenario loop; both also compare errors and ignore forged prices/tier. A covers a multi-product basket while B checks duplicate lines exceeding stock. Neither difference establishes an overall advantage.

uncertainties: Neither added suite independently tests the coupon floor after lowering product prices, although both reuse the unchanged authoritative pricing implementation.
Reported test execution was not independently confirmed.

Both keep a single pricing rule and a small read-only route. The serialization/annotation choice is not a meaningful maintainability advantage here.

B/tests/test_quotes.py:27-126 covers the same main contracts, adding an explicit insufficient-stock quote case and exact shipping boundary while A exercises duplicate-line quote/order parity. Both provide substantial independent checks.

uncertainties: FastAPI serialization behavior and reported passing runs were inspected through source and reports, not independently executed.

reasons.message: Correctness and maintainability: A acquires BEGIN IMMEDIATE before shared visibility and saved-key checks, groups quantities by product, and includes stock/history/status/key changes in one connection transaction. B/store/orders.py:21-57 follows the same sequence and policy ownership. Added parameter annotations in A do not establish a material advantage.

Verification: A injects failures at all write stages and deferred commit, and checks concurrent same-key, different-key and different-order requests. B/tests/test_cancellation.py:106-163 checks all write stages and the same race categories; B:83-85 additionally tests visibility loss before replay. The distinct extra cases are useful, but both verify the requested transaction and concurrency contracts comprehensively.

uncertainties: No behavior defect identified from static inspection; concurrency outcomes, validator behavior and reported runs were not independently executed.
SQLite lock waiting still uses the fixture's existing 10-second timeout on both sides.

reasons.message: Correctness and contracts: A uses re.fullmatch for the required ASCII key rule; B/store/api.py:26-33 declares length and pattern validation on Header. Both enforce the requested rule at the API boundary with 422 failures. B exposes constraints declaratively, but the small explicit validation in A remains readily understandable.

Ownership and locality: A and B/store/orders.py:21 both reuse require_visible_order and serialize all cancellation reads/writes inside BEGIN IMMEDIATE and a connection transaction. A writes the status after stock/history; B writes it first. All writes remain in one transaction, so this sequencing does not establish a correctness difference.

Verification: A's failure at the final key insert checks rollback of all preceding changes, plus same-key and new-key concurrency. B/tests/test_cancellation.py:107-159 exercises individual write failures and simultaneous key reuse across orders as well. B has broader race-specific coverage; A still checks the core rollback and retry requirements. This is a modest coverage difference, insufficient to outweigh otherwise equivalent implementation quality.

uncertainties: B's anchored Header pattern uses Pydantic's configured validator, whereas A uses Python fullmatch; both suites include trailing-newline cases, but neither run was independently executed.
Neither candidate supplies a deferred-commit failure check. This is a verification limit, not an identified transaction defect.

reasons.message: Correctness and contracts: A places required key constraints in Header; B/store/api.py:27-31 checks the equivalent ASCII/length rule with fullmatch. Both keep validation at the route and delegate the transaction. A's declarative validation and B's explicit validation are reasonable small implementations.

Ownership and side effects: A and B/store/orders.py:21-54 use the same shared order visibility rule, write-lock-before-read discipline, saved user-key response, grouped product quantities and single transaction. Formatting and comment differences do not change understanding of the operation.

Verification: A explicitly replays through a new application instance and injects failure at each write table. B/tests/test_cancel.py:92-142 checks partial multi-product failure and three concurrency cases, where A checks concurrent matching retries only. Both verify the stated primary contracts; their complementary checks do not establish a material overall maintainability difference.

uncertainties: A does not exercise concurrent conflicting keys; B does not exercise failure at the order-status write. Both are coverage limits rather than demonstrated behavior defects.
Reported passing runs and regex-validator behavior were not independently executed.

reasons.message: Correctness and policy ownership: A builds count and page predicates from visibility_clause and binds status/limit/offset. B/store/orders.py:10-29 uses the same policy and parameter binding. A skips the page query when offset exceeds total; B clamps the SQL offset to total while returning the original offset. Both handle an empty page and very large offsets correctly for the requested use.

Contracts and locality: B supplies OrderSummary/OrderPage response models and A returns the explicitly selected summary dictionaries. B's models describe the response while A's short projection is directly inspectable; neither introduces a redundant policy or an unnecessary service layer. Added models alone do not determine a winner.

Verification: A compares visibility with detail access for every fixture actor and checks filtered count, pagination, empty/large-offset pages and invalid/auth inputs. B/tests/test_order_list.py:33-94 supplies comparable independent expected results and adds an owner-matching order in another tenant. Both meaningfully test the requested boundaries.

uncertainties: Neither candidate promises a single snapshot spanning the count and page SELECTs under concurrent writes; that behavior was not requested and no advantage is inferred.
Reports of passing runs were not independently confirmed.

reasons.message: Correctness and maintainability: A and B/store/orders.py:7-24 derive both SQL statements from the existing visibility predicate, bind user values, count before pagination and avoid binding oversized offsets when the page is empty. A uses an early return; B initializes items then conditionally queries. These are equivalent small control flows.

Contracts: A's OrderSummary/OrdersPage models and B/store/schemas.py:14-24 describe the same fields and types and are used as response models by their routes. Different page-class names and added argument annotations in B have no material effect on future changes.

Verification: A checks exact actor-specific IDs and detail projections, status before pagination, retained counts, giant offsets, errors and authentication. B/tests/test_order_list.py:34-115 covers those same contracts and adds a matching-owner/cross-tenant row. Different grouping/test counts do not demonstrate an overall quality difference.

uncertainties: The reported passing test runs were not independently executed.
Count/page consistency during concurrent writes was not tested on either side; the task does not require that additional guarantee.

reasons.message: Correctness and ownership: A and B/store/orders.py:7-23 use the same visibility predicate and parameterized status/count/page queries, descending IDs and empty-page handling for huge offsets. Early-return versus conditional-query structure makes no material difference here.

Readability and contracts: B adds explicit response models and a named OrderStatus alias; A/store/api.py:19-27 validates the same query contract with an inline Literal and returns the explicitly projected dictionary. Both flows are clear and local. Models and annotations alone do not justify preferring B.

Verification: A independently checks the full response, all actor roles, agreement with detail visibility, filtered pagination and totals, oversized offsets, errors and injection inputs. B/tests/test_order_list.py:35-120 adds an actual result set exceeding the default page size and a matching-owner/cross-tenant row. Those strengthen specific regressions, while A already verifies limit slicing and both policy clauses. The extra cases do not establish a material overall quality gap.

uncertainties: Passing runs in both reports were not independently confirmed.
A does not independently exercise the default page size against more than 20 rows; B does. This is a coverage difference, not an identified defect in A.

limits: Read only the fixed rubric, shared fixture and anonymized task/candidate files within blind/pair-1 through pair-9. Did not inspect mappings, protocols, graders, original runs, other reviewer outputs, skills or network resources.

Static review only. A preliminary attempt to invoke the default python command failed because it resolved to an inaccessible WindowsApps alias; no candidate code or tests were executed and no runtime pass/fail claims are made here.
Original fixture files were compared by content hashes; changed source, added tests and candidate reports were read. The original regression tests were unchanged in all candidates.

No material behavior defect was identified by static inspection in these pairs. Ties reflect close implementation quality and adequate comparable checks, not proof that either implementation is defect-free.
Scores are exploratory ordinal AI judgments under this rubric, not measured developer review time or evidence of universal productivity differences.
